The '''Animal Justice Party Aotearoa New Zealand''' ('''AJP''') is a registered political party in [[New Zealand]]. The party advocates non-violence towards animals, sustainability, and a move away from animal-based agriculture.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/top/494780/on-the-campaign-trail-era-reforms-gang-talk-moving-ports-and-animal-rights |title=On the campaign trail: ERA reforms, gang talk, moving ports and animal rights |publisher=[[RNZ]] |date=30 July 2023 |access-date=17 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.times.co.nz/election-2023/new-political-party-focusing-on-animal-welfare-issues/ |title=New political party focusing on animal welfare issues |publisher=Eastern Times |date=3 October 2023 |access-date=10 April 2025}}</ref>

==History==
The AJP was founded after discussions with the [[Animal Justice Party]] in Australia, who also gave permission to use the name.  The original policies of the AJP were closely aligned with the Australian party, but have since been extensively revised and expanded to reflect New Zealand, and coverage of animal, planet and people issues.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy-browser/|title=AJP Policies}}</ref> AJPANZ was registered as an Incorporated Society on 11 November 2022.<ref name=IncRec/> In May 2023 the party was granted $66,332 in broadcasting funding for the [[2023 New Zealand general election]], provisional upon registration.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2023/2023-broadcasting-allocation-decision/ |title=2023 broadcasting allocation decision |publisher=Electoral Commission |date=12 May 2023 |access-date=17 August 2023 |archive-date=29 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230829142714/https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2023/2023-broadcasting-allocation-decision/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The party applied for registration with the Electoral Commission on 31 July 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2023/application-to-register-political-party-and-logo-2/ |title=Application to Register Political Party and Logo |publisher=Electoral Commission |date=31 July 2023 |access-date=17 August 2023}}</ref> It was registered on 16 August 2023.<ref name="NZEC2023b">{{cite web |url=https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2023/two-parties-approved-for-registration/ |title=Two parties approved for registration  |publisher=Electoral Commission |date=16 August 2023 |access-date=16 August 2023}}</ref>

== Policies and ideology ==

=== Animals ===
The AJP says they believe that all animals, regardless of form, deserve the [[Right to life|right to live]] and thrive. They say that animals currently face cruel, inadequate and exploitative conditions that prioritise human interests over their inherent rights and well-being. They advocate for systemic change, regulatory reforms and safeguards that prioritise the rights and value of non human life.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Policy Browser – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy-browser/ |access-date=2025-04-10 |website=animaljustice.org.nz |archive-date=1 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250401083521/https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy-browser/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

They would:

* Ban [[recreational fishing]] and fishing competitions<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ban recreational fishing and fishing competitions – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/recreational-fishing/ |access-date=2025-04-10 |website=animaljustice.org.nz}}</ref>
* Ban the use of all [[Animals in sport|animals for entertainment]], while supporting the people in the industry to find new jobs<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ending the Use of All Animals for 'Entertainment' – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/ending-animals-entertainment/ |access-date=2025-04-10 |website=animaljustice.org.nz}}</ref>
* Support the ban on [[greyhound racing]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ban Greyhound Racing – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/greyhounds/ |access-date=2025-04-10 |website=animaljustice.org.nz |archive-date=4 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250204103535/https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/greyhounds/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
* Ban all forms of [[horse racing]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ban Horse Racing – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/horse-racing/ |access-date=2025-04-10 |website=animaljustice.org.nz |archive-date=4 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250204103622/https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/horse-racing/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
* Ban [[rodeo]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ban Rodeo – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/rodeo/ |access-date=2025-04-10 |website=animaljustice.org.nz |archive-date=4 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250204103734/https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/rodeo/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
* Ban recreational hunting and hunting competitions<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ban Recreational Hunting and Hunting Competitions – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/hunting/ |access-date=2025-04-10 |website=animaljustice.org.nz |archive-date=10 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250710224527/https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/hunting/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
* Create compassionate and sick leave for companion animal death and sickness<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |title=Companion animals – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/companion-animals/ |access-date=2025-09-06 |website=animaljustice.org.nz}}</ref>
* Support pets on public transport<ref name=":7" />
* End the commercial breeding of companion animals<ref name=":7" />
* End intensive winter grazing<ref>{{Cite web |title=End Intensive Winter Grazing – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/intensive-winter-grazing/ |access-date=2025-09-06 |website=animaljustice.org.nz}}</ref>
* Conduct a full and independent review is undertaken of the treatment of calves viewed through the lens of the calf and that review be publicly shared<ref>{{Cite web |title=Calves born into the dairy Industry – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/calves-born-into-the-dairy-industry/ |access-date=2025-09-06 |website=animaljustice.org.nz}}</ref>
* Ban the production of fur and leather<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fur and leather – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/fur-and-leather/ |access-date=2025-09-06 |website=animaljustice.org.nz}}</ref>
* Ban animal experimentation<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ending Animal Experimentation – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/animal-experimentation/ |access-date=2025-09-06 |website=animaljustice.org.nz}}</ref>
* Oppose the use of 1080<ref>{{Cite web |title=Animal control – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/unwanted-animal-control/ |access-date=2025-09-06 |website=animaljustice.org.nz}}</ref>
* Appoint a commissioner for animals with legal jurisdiction over animal well-being, enabling monitoring of all sectors<ref>{{Cite web |title=Commissioner for Animals – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/animal-rights-commissioner/ |access-date=2025-09-06 |website=animaljustice.org.nz}}</ref>

=== Environment and economy ===
The AJP wants to switch to a plant-based economy that respects sentient animals. It states that climate change is one of the most urgent challenges we face, and that it is caused by [[greenhouse gas emissions]] from burning [[Fossil fuel|fossil fuels]], the destruction of natural ecosystems and [[intensive animal farming]]. It calls for urgent action on [[climate change]] and a phased switch to [[Plant-based diet|plant based diets]].<ref name=":1" />

They would:

* Reduce greenhouse gas emissions by transitioning to a plant-based economy, supporting farmers to grow produce instead of farming animals<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Urgently addressing climate change – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/urgently-addressing-climate-change/ |access-date=2025-04-18 |website=animaljustice.org.nz |archive-date=10 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250710232642/https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/urgently-addressing-climate-change/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
* Support policies that reduce emissions, avoid unnecessary animal suffering, improve human and non-human animal health, and restore and expand our waterways, forests and wildlife<ref name=":2" />
* Advocate for a paradigm shift in agriculture towards efficient and productive land use without farming animals<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Protecting ecosystems and biodiversity – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/ecosystems/ |access-date=2025-04-18 |website=animaljustice.org.nz |archive-date=10 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250710233405/https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/ecosystems/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
* Support compassionate conservation measures, habitat restoration, and the implementation of policies to mitigate the impact of pollutants and pesticides<ref name=":3" />
* Embrace the concept of Kaitiakitanga, recognising our responsibility as guardians of the land<ref name=":3" />
* Promote the adoption of circular economy principles, community-led initiatives, and local resilience measures to minimise negative impact on the ecological footprint<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Economic sufficiency within planetary boundaries – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/economic-sufficiency/ |access-date=2025-04-18 |website=animaljustice.org.nz}}</ref>
* Envision a society that measures success, not only by economic metrics, but also by the health of ecosystems, the well being of communities, and the ethical and moral treatment of non-human animals<ref name=":4" />
* Banning factory farming<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Transition to a plant-based economy – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/plant-based-economy/ |access-date=2025-04-18 |website=animaljustice.org.nz}}</ref>
* Enact tougher laws, regulations and enforcement mechanisms regarding animal farming<ref name=":5" />
* Support farm livelihood transitions<ref name=":5" />
* Support innovation in food tech<ref name=":5" />
* Aims to eliminate food waste and environmental pollution while reducing energy and material use <ref name=":8">{{Cite web |title=Waste and pollution – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/waste-and-pollution/ |access-date=2025-09-06 |website=animaljustice.org.nz}}</ref>
* Support recycling<ref name=":8" />
* Make changes to commercial fishing to reduce plastic pollution and by-catch<ref name=":8" />
* Encourage reuse, recycling and composting programs in businesses and public institutions<ref name=":8" />
* Stop the dumping of edible food by retailers and to ensure these products are sent to people in need<ref name=":8" />
* Prioritise rewilding of farmland and expansion of wetlands<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |title=Biodiversity – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/biodiversity/ |access-date=2025-09-06 |website=animaljustice.org.nz}}</ref>
* Require councils to protect significant trees and will ensure that there are wildlife corridors in urban areas<ref name=":9" />

=== People ===
The AJP seeks to create a society where the [[Welfare spending|welfare]], and ability to thrive, of both humans and other animals is at the forefront, guided by compassion, inclusivity, just governance, and a commitment to sustainability.<ref name=":1" />

They would:

* Embrace the Treaty of Waitangi and acknowledge its importance in guiding a compassionate, just and equitable relationship with animals<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=Te Tiriti o Waitangi – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/policy/te-tiriti-o-waitangi/ |access-date=2025-04-18 |website=animaljustice.org.nz}}</ref>
* Reflect the essence of Te Tiriti o Waitangi, promoting harmony and respect for all beings within the nation’s diverse tapestry<ref name=":6" />
* Promote and incentivise more compassionate and healthy dietary choices<ref name=":5" />
* Teach children about the importance of biodiversity<ref name=":9" />
* Support the protection efforts of tangata whenua towards the use and care of natural resources<ref>{{Cite web |title=Te Tiriti o Waitangi – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/treaty-of-waitangi/ |access-date=2025-09-06 |website=animaljustice.org.nz}}</ref>

== Advocacy ==
In addition to being a political party, the AJP also acts as somewhat of an advocacy group, hosting petitions for or against government actions.

=== Mud farming ===
Mud farming, also known as intensive winter grazing, is a practice where animals are confined over winter to outdoor feeding areas planted with annual forage crops.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Industries |first=Ministry for Primary |date=2025-04-15 |title=Intensive winter grazing {{!}} NZ Government |url=https://www.mpi.govt.nz/agriculture/farm-management-the-environment-and-land-use/protecting-freshwater-health/intensive-winter-grazing/ |access-date=2025-05-03 |website=Intensive winter grazing {{!}} NZ Government |language=en-NZ |archive-date=3 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250403173335/https://www.mpi.govt.nz/agriculture/farm-management-the-environment-and-land-use/protecting-freshwater-health/intensive-winter-grazing |url-status=live }}</ref> AJPANZ claims that it causes immense harm to animals and our environment and created a template to send a submissions to government ministers and the [[Mayor of Southland District|Southland mayor]], urging them to thoroughly investigate farms to ensure they aren't mud farming and to establish a Minister for Animals to enforce [[Animal Welfare Act 1999|animal welfare laws]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Demand for Investigation: Southland Animal Suffering Exposed |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/campaign/southland-mud-farming/ |access-date=2025-05-03 |website=animaljustice.org.nz |language=en-NZ |archive-date=12 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250612221441/https://animaljustice.org.nz/campaign/southland-mud-farming/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Live export ===
[[Live export|Live exporting]] is the practice of shipping living livestock overseas by sea. It has been illegal in New Zealand since April of 2023, the [[Sixth National Government of New Zealand|current coalition government]] has promised to overturn that ban. AJPANZ has a petition urging the government to keep the ban and it also hopes to convince individual ports, local councils and the global community to take policy positions against live export.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sign the Public Appeal |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/campaign/stop-live-export/ |access-date=2025-05-03 |website=animaljustice.org.nz |language=en-NZ |archive-date=20 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250520135425/https://animaljustice.org.nz/campaign/stop-live-export/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Election results and support ==
===National===
In the run up to the 2023 New Zealand general election, the party announced they had reached 1000 followers on Facebook and 280 party members.<ref>{{Cite web |title=We're Growing! – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/were-growing/ |access-date=2025-03-31 |website=animaljustice.org.nz |archive-date=16 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250116122325/https://animaljustice.org.nz/were-growing/ |url-status=live }}</ref> 

The party ran 17 candidates in the [[2023 New Zealand general election]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/kahu/election-2023-animal-rights-leads-to-youngest-and-oldest-candidates-for-animal-justice-party/ZU7LWVYJCJEIPLUUPWNSG76BKI/ |title=Election 2023: Animal rights leads to youngest and oldest candidates for Animal Justice Party |publisher=[[New Zealand Herald]] |date=12 October 2023 |access-date=13 October 2023 |archive-date=13 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231013014633/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/kahu/election-2023-animal-rights-leads-to-youngest-and-oldest-candidates-for-animal-justice-party/ZU7LWVYJCJEIPLUUPWNSG76BKI/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Two polls conducted for 1 News in September 2023 indicated that support for the Animal Justice Party was around 0.3 to 0.4 percent.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1News Verian Poll Report September 16–19 |url=https://www.scribd.com/document/672428933/1News-Verian-Poll-Report-September-16-19 |access-date=2023-09-23 |website=Scribd |language=en |archive-date=5 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231005041631/https://www.scribd.com/document/672428933/1News-Verian-Poll-Report-September-16-19 |url-status=live }}</ref>  The party ultimately received 0.17% of the party vote, earning no seats.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 General Election - Official Result |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/index.html |website=Electoral Commission |access-date=3 November 2023 |archive-date=4 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231104213043/https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

The party ran a candidate in the [[2023 Port Waikato by-election]], coming fourth.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Sowman-Lund |first=Stewart |date=2023-10-20 |title=Port Waikato byelection: Full candidate list unveiled, Act also not standing |url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/live-updates/20-10-2023/port-waikato-byelection-full-candidate-list-unveiled-act-also-not-standing |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=[[The Spinoff]] |language=en}}</ref>

In an August 2025 national poll, the AJP registered at 1% support for the first time. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Poll: Labour surges, Luxon's popularity hits two-year low |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2025/08/11/poll-labour-surges-luxons-popularity-hits-two-year-low/ |access-date=14 August 2025 |archive-date=14 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250814113215/https://www.1news.co.nz/2025/08/11/poll-labour-surges-luxons-popularity-hits-two-year-low/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The party will be contesting electorates and the party list in the 2026 national election.{{cn|date=March 2026}}

===Local===
In the [[2025 New Zealand local elections|2025 local elections]], the party unsuccessfully stood candidates for mayor [[2025 Auckland mayoral election|in Auckland]]<ref>{{cite news |last1=Donnell |first1=Hayden |title=The motley crew of contenders trying to take down Auckland mayor Wayne Brown |url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/12-08-2025/the-motley-crew-of-contenders-trying-to-take-down-auckland-mayor-wayne-brown |access-date=14 August 2025 |work=[[The Spinoff]] |date=12 August 2025 |language=en}}</ref> and [[2025 Hamilton mayoral election|in Hamilton]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waiwiri-Smith |first1=Lyric |title=Who wants to be the next mayor of Hamilton? |url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/06-08-2025/who-wants-to-be-the-next-mayor-of-hamilton |access-date=14 August 2025 |work=[[The Spinoff]] |date=6 August 2025 |language=en}}</ref> and for seats on the [[2025 Whanganui District Council election|Whanganui District Council]] and the Bay of Plenty Regional Council.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Evans |first1=Alisha |title=Local Elections 2025: Bay of Plenty Regional Council candidates announced |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/bay-of-plenty-times/news/local-elections-2025-bay-of-plenty-regional-council-candidates-announced/O6ZGVNQ5A5BKFFFPH4JFC6BOQ4/ |access-date=14 August 2025 |work=[[Bay of Plenty Times]] |agency=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=5 August 2025 |language=en-NZ}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Our Candidates – Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |url=https://animaljustice.org.nz/our-candidates/ |website=animaljustice.org.nz |publisher=Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ |access-date=14 August 2025 |archive-date=14 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250814113121/https://animaljustice.org.nz/our-candidates/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
